records.qtitle: Number of unmanned railway level crossings
records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text: (a)    the number of unmanned railway level crossings across the country;<br/><br/>  (b)    whether Government has established a nation-wide database of the number of fatal accidents occurring at the unmanned railway level crossings, if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>  (c)    whether Government plans to install warning systems at the unmanned railway level crossings to prevent fatal accidents?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI MANOJ SINHA)<br/><br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c):  A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text: (a)	 whether Government plans to formulate a National Optical Fibre Network (NOFN) Policy, if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(b)	 whether Government plans to adopt uniform Right of Way (RoW) measures for greater involvement of States in the policy;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether Government plans to release more spectrum for successful rollout of wireless broadband, ensuring seamless execution of the NOFN policy; and<br/><br/>(d)	 whether Government plans to connect Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to National Internet Exchange of India (NIXI), making it an effective Internet Exchange Point (IXP), if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY<br/>(SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD)<br/>	<br/>(a) & (b)	National Optical Fibre Network (NOFN) was planned, in 2011, to connect all the 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) in the country through optical fibre utilizing existing fibres of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) viz. Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL), RailTel and Power Grid and laying incremental fibre wherever necessary to bridge the connectivity gap between Gram Panchayats and Blocks, for providing broadband connectivity by all categories of service providers on non-discriminatory basis. The project is being executed by a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) namely, Bharat Broadband Network Limited (BBNL), which has been incorporated on 25.02.2012 under Indian Companies Act 1956.<br/><br/>NOFN Project was envisaged as a Centre-State joint effort. State Governments are expected to contribute by way of not levying any Right of Way (RoW) charges. This requires suitable Tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to be signed by Central Government, State Governments & Bharat Broadband Network Limited (BBNL). Tripartite MoU has been signed with all the States and Union Territories except Tamil Nadu and Lakshadweep. <br/><br/>(c)	Spectrum available in various frequency bands for telecommunication services including wireless broadband, put for auction conducted from time to time, has increased the availability of spectrum with telecom service providers. Based on the reference made by Government, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released a Consultation paper dated 26.11.2015 on valuation and reserve price of spectrum in 700 Megahertz(MHz), 800 MHz, 900 MHz, 1800 MHz, 2100 MHz and 2500 MHz band for the next round of auction of spectrum. <br/><br/>(d)	Government has setup National Internet Exchange of India (NIXI) nodes at various locations in the country for Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to connect.  At present, 43 ISPs at 7 locations (Mumbai, Delhi, Chennai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Ahmedabad) are already connected with NIXI. With increasing data traffic, it is expected more number of ISPs will get connected at these NIXI nodes.<br/>

records.qtitle: Private entities to manufacture space related equipment
records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government plans to incubate private entities manufacturing space related equipments under ''Make in India'' scheme, if so, details thereof;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether Government plans to allow active collaboration between the Earth Sciences and Space Ministries for developing disaster mitigation techniques; and<br/><br/>(c) 	whether Government has carried out timely appraisals of the remote sensing data policy, if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PG & PENSIONS AND IN THE PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE<br/>(DR. JITENDRA SINGH):<br/><br/>(a)	ISRO is making focussed efforts to consolidate and enhance participation of Indian industries including private entities in the manufacture of space related hardware such as rocket engine & stages, propellant tanks, spacecraft structures, solar panels, thermal control systems etc., required for satellites and launch vehicles. It is envisaged that the industry will have enhanced contribution towards manufacture of standardised components as well as integrated systems /subsystems through appropriate consortium.<br/><br/>(b)	Yes Sir. Ministry of Earth Sciences and Department of Space are collaborating for developing disaster mitigation techniques for accurate forecasting of cyclone track & intensity, heavy rainfall alerts, fog, inundation scenarios in the coastal areas and in establishment of Tsunami & Storm Surge Warning Centre and Doppler Weather Radars. <br/><br/>(c)	Yes Sir. Taking note of advances in imaging capability with high spatial resolution, both at national and global level and prevailing security considerations, Government has carried out an appraisal of the then existing RSDP 2001 and positioned new/revised RSDP 2011 with a view to ensure availability of high resolution data for developmental purposes. RSDP 2011, permits distribution of all satellite data of resolutions up to 1 m (as compared to 5.8 m in RSDP 2001) on a non-discriminatory and “as requested basis” to the user; and all data of better than 1 m resolution after screening and clearance by the appropriate agency prior to distribution.<br/><br/>*****

records.qtitle: Classification of weaker section for Housing for All scheme
records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether Government plans to establish a robust criteria for classification of weaker sections, for affordable housing, under Housing for All scheme 2022; and <br/><br/>(b) whether Government plans to elucidate on the mandatory conditions for easing up of urban land market for providing adequate land for affordable housing, under the same?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING & URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION<br/>               [SHRI BABUL SUPRIYO]<br/><br/><br/>(a):	 Under the “Housing for All (Urban)” Mission launched on 25.6.2015, Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) have been defined as urban poor with annual household income upto Rs. 3 lakhs and Low Income Group (LIG) with annual household income between 3-6 lakhs. <br/><br/>(b):	Land and Colonization are State subjects and it is for them to assess the land requirement for housing projects.  Availability of urban land is, however, the biggest constraint in providing housing to all including weaker sections.  In order to ease administrative bottlenecks, a set of Mandatory Conditions have been included in the “Housing for All (Urban)” Mission to facilitate growth of housing sector including affordable housing.  For participating in the Mission and to avail of financial assistance from Central Government, States/ UTs should agree to fulfil Mandatory Conditions prescribed under Mission Guidelines.<br/>                      ******<br/>

records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are aware of widespread corruption in the Canteen Stores Department regarding purchase of various items that are canalized through this organization;

(b) if so, whether the norms for the purchase of the alcoholic beverages are consistent with overall purchase policies or whether there are different norms governing such purchases; and

(c) whether the Servicemen are receiving their wide choice of products that are available in the market or whether the Canteen Stores Department purchase organization is restricting the choice through their restrictive purchase policies?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES)


(a) All the purchases in the Canteen Stores Department are made as per laid down norms and policies. However, as and when any case of corrupt practice comes to notice, necessary action is initiated as per rules.

(b) The norms for the purchase of the alcoholic beverages in canteen stores department are consistent with overall purchase policies.

(c) Canteen Stores Department provides wide choice of products keeping in view the requirement of the consumer.

records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Indian Airlines propose to purchase new passenger aircraft;

(b) if so, which make/model of aircraft is proposed to be purchased;

(c) what has been the evaluation procedure prior to deciding on the make/model of the aircraft proposed to be purchased;

(d) what are the type of engines proposed to be purchased along with such aircraft; and

(e) the evaluation procedure in respect of the selection of the engines?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY )
(a),(b),(c),(d) and (e): Indian Airlines has submitted a Project Report for acquisition of 43 aircraft comprising Airbus A-319, Airbus A-320 and Airbus A-321. The proposed aircraft are to be fitted with CFM-56 engines. The selection of the aircraft/ engines are based on techno-economic evaluation of offers received from aircraft and engine manufacturers.

records.name: Vijay Mallya
records.qn_text:
(a) the total strength of aircrafts owned and operated by Indian Airlines at present;

(b) the number of aircrafts which have outlived their normal lives and require replacement;

(c) whether it is a fact that Government are considering a proposal for purchase of 43 aircrafts at a cost of Rs.10,000 crores instead of obtaining them on wet/dry lease;

(d) whether any study on traffic growth has been undertaken which would justify purchase of these aircrafts instead of taking them on wet/dry lease; and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY )
(a): Indian Airlines has a fleet of 47 owned aircraft. (b): There is no prescribed upper age for commercial aircraft. However, the aircraft have a design economic life beyond which the operation becomes uneconomical due to the increasing maintenance cost. (c): The project report of Indian Airlines for acquisition of 43 aircraft at the cost of Rs.10,089 crores has since been received. (d) and (e): The working group on Civil Aviation for the Tenth Five Year Plan has projected average annual growth rate in domestic passenger traffic to be of 5% and that in international passenger traffic to be of 6%. The new aircraft are envisaged to replace the entire fleet of A-300 and B-737-200 in a phased manner by March, 2005 as well as to cater to the projected traffic growth during the five year period.

records.qtitle: PENALISING IMPACT OF SUBSIDY CUT ON PRIVATE FERTILIZER PLANTS .
records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that heavy losses are being sustained by most of the public sector fertilizer plants year after year which were as high as Rs. 2,466 crore in the year 2001-02, as per the report of the Ministry; and

(b) whether Government are subsidizing such losses, at the same time trying to save much smaller amounts on subsidy, by penalizing the efficiency of private and cooperative sector fertilizer plants, under the garb of reducing subsidy, if so, how government expect to ensure continued health and viability of efficiently run fertilizer plants ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR)

(a): There are 8 Public Sector Undertakings under the administrative control of the Department of Fertilizers. Out of these, 5 companies including 4 sick companies, reported losses for 2001-02. The total loss reported by these companies for 2001-02 is Rs. 2142.48 crore.

(b): Parameters/norms, governing the determination of subsidy payments, are applied uniformly to all urea manufacturing units, whether they are in private sector, public sector or cooperative sector.

records.qtitle: NEW BILATERAL AGREEMENT OF AI WITH MALAYSIAN AND EMIRATES AIRLINES .
records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Air India has signed any new bilateral agreement with Emirates recently; and

(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV)

(a) and (b): During last round of bilateral air services consultation between India and United Arab Emirates (Dubai) held in Delhi on 19-20th April, 2001, Hyderabad has been granted as an additional point of call to the designated airline of Dubai, i.e., Emirates with a separate entitlement of 2000 seats per week. Capacity entitlement for the designated airline of India has also been enhanced by 2000 seats per week. This was done with a view to reduce congestion and to provide better connectivity to the newly declared international airport of Hyderabad. Emirates` operations between Dubai and Hyderabad would be covered by their existing pool agreement with Air India.



(b) if so, the reasons why Hindustan Lever Ltd., which was also convicted by SEBI, allowed to bid for and subsequently to take over Modern Food last year ?

MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DISINVESTMENT, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRIES OF PLANNING, STATISTICS & PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC GRIEVANCES.

(SHRI ARUN SHOURIE)

a) No, Sir.
b) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: SUBJECT CUSTOMS DUTY ON AUDIO MAGNETIC TAPES
records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text:
(a)Whether it is a fact that Customs duty on inputs for manufacture of Audio Magnetic Tape is 38.5 per cent whereas it is 20 per cent for imported finished products.;

(b) whether Government are aware that this inverted duty structure is gross discrimination against the domestic industry resulting in closure of more than 50 per cent units in the last decade and many more are on the verge of closure;

(c) whether Government have received representations from the industry to bring down duty on inputs down to zero percent to make it competitive; and

(d) if so, what action Government propose to take to correct these anomalies and by when?
records.ans_text:
(a): The major inputs used in the manufacture of Audio Magnetic Tapes are Polyester Films, Polyurethane Elastomer and Gamma Ferric Oxide. While the import duty on Gamma Ferric Oxide is 16.5% ad valorem (inclusive of surcharge), the import duty on the other inputs mentioned above is 38.5% ad valorem (inclusive of surcharge). The import duty on Audio Magnetic Tape is 20% ad valorem.

(b),(c) and (d): Information available with the Government for 1998 and 1999 does not indicate any decline in the production of audio magnetic tapes . The Government have received representations from the industry requesting for reduction in import duty on inputs used in the manufacture of audio magnetic tapes to a level of 5% ad valorem. The representations will be examined as part of the Budget exercise for the year 2001-2002.

records.qtitle: LONG TERM POLICY TO TACKLE NATURAL CALAMITIES .
records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that State of Gujarat had worst drought very recently and had approached Government for financial assistance;

(b) if so, the quantum of assistance sought and the amount sanctioned disbursed;

(c) whether Government contemplate to form some long-term policy so that these types of natural calamities could be controlled/fought effectively; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SBPBK SATYANARAYANA RAO)


(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) During 1999-2000, in addition to release of entire Central share of Calamity Relief Fund (CRF) amounting to Rs.121.05 crore, Rs.54.58 crore (against Rs.722.16 crore demanded) was released to the State from the National Fund for Calamity Relief (NFCR). During 2000-01, three quarterly instalments of Central share of CRF amounting to Rs.131.14 crore have also been released to the State.

(c)&(d) Funds are also released under the schemes like Drought Prone Areas Programme. Desert Development Programme and Employment Generation Schemes, Accelerated Rural Water Supply Programme, Indira Awas Yojana, Flood Control Scheme, National Watershed Development Project for Rainfed Areas and Soil Conservation in the Catchments of River Valley Project and Flood Prone Rivers implemented by the Centrtal Ministries/Departments, which have components of disaster mitigation, towards long-term rehabilitation measures in the wake of natural calamities.

records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has been sudden spurt of attacks and violence on minorities and their places of worship in various parts of the country recently;

(b) if so, the details of such incidents during the last twelve months;

(c) whether Government have obtained reports from the concerned State Governments, and if so, the details thereof; and

(d) the steps taken/proposed to be taken by Government to ensure safety and security of the minorities and their institutions?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( I.D.SWAMI)

A Statement is laid on the table of the House. < RSSQ NO. 52 FOR 26.7.2000 Statement referred to in reply to (a) to (d) on Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 52 on 26.7.2000


(a)&(b): No sir, there is no overall increase in the incidents of violence involving the minorities and their institutions in the country during the last few years. However, incidents of violence involving Christians and their institutions have increased to some extent. As per available information, incidents and persons killed/injured during the period 1998 upto June, 2000 are at Annexures-I & II.

( c): Reports have been obtained from the State Government in cases of major incidents. With regard to the series of bomb blasts in church premises in the State of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Goa, the involvement of activists of an organization called the Deendar Anjuman has been established. Cases have been registered under relevant provisions of law by the concerned States.

(d): As per the provisions of the VII Scheduled, List II - State List of the Constitution of India, law and order is a State subject. However, the Central Government shares intelligence inputs and sends advisories and alert messages to the States from time to time. Revised guidelines for the promotion of communal harmony have been issued in October, 1997. A high level meeting was convened on 4.7.2000 to review the situation. records.qtitle: FINALISATION OF DEFENCE DEAL WITH RUSSIA .
records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have finalised a Defence Deal with Russia to acquire T-90 tanks and “KIEV” class naval aircraft during the recent visit of the Defence Minister to Russia;

(b) if so, the details of the discussions held and decisions taken; and

(c) the impact on our Defence expenditure?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES)


(a) No, Sir.

(b) & (c): Do not arise.

records.qtitle: CASES PENDING WITH INCOME TAX APPELLATE TRIBUNAL .
records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text:
(a) the number of cases pending with Income Tax Appellate Tribunal as on date;

(b) the number of cases where amount exceeds Rs. 1 crore or more;

(c) whether Government are contemplating early disposal of the same to avoid loss of revenue and harassment of the assesses involved; and

(d) the steps to be taken in this regard and time-frame, any thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) AND MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW, JUSTICE & COMPANY AFFAIRS ( SHRI ARUN JAITLEY )

(a) The number of cases pending with Income-tax Appellate Tribunal as on 1.7.2000 is 2,61,317.

(b), (c) & (d) Income-tax Appellate Tribunal does not maintain any consolidated/common record of the appeals regarding the amount involved in each appeal. However, in order to reduce the pendency of the appeals, the Government has sanctioned 15 additional Benches. Of these, ten benches have started functioning. Appointment of Members to fill the vacancies have already been taken up. 19 Members are in the process of joining. Remaining vacancies have already been advertised.
.....

records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text:
(a) whether a Draft Civil Aviation Policy is under the consideration of Government;

(b) if so, what are the primary objectives of the proposed policy and by what time the policy is likely to be formulated;

(c) whether it is a fact that there are serious differences about creation of Civil Aviation Authority;

(d) if so, the details and functions of Authority; and

(e) what would be the future role of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation and Bureau of Civil Aviation Security in the event of creation of Civil Aviation Authority.
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV)

(a): Yes, Sir.



(b) to (e): The draft Civil Aviation Policy, seeks to set up a policy framework to promote efficient, cost effective and orderly growth of air transport, ensure safety and security in accordance with international standard and generate a healthy competitive civil aviation environment which contribute to social and economic development of the country. This policy document is being finalised and will be announced in the near future.


records.qtitle: POOR QUALITY OF SERVICE OFFERED BY AI AND IA .
records.name: Praful Patel
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Indian Airlines and Air India have accumulated losses over the years;

(b) whether it is also a fact that performance and quality of service to the passengers have nose-dived over the years and there have been mounting complaints in this regard;

(c) whether Government have been contemplating partial privatisation of both the airlines; and

(d) if so; the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): There is scope for improvement. Both the airlines constantly endeavour to bring about improvements in the services rendered to the passengers both on the ground and in the air.

(c) & (d) :The Government has approved in principle, bringing down the equity of the Government of India in Air India to 40% through a process of disinvestment by sale of 40% of equity to a strategic partner, upto 10% to employees and the balance by sale to financial institutions and/or on the share market. In the event of the strategic partner being a joint venture with an element of foreign holding, the arrangement should be such as would limit foreign holding in Air India to a maximum of 26% of the total equity.
As regards, Indian Airlines, Government has decided to disinvest 51 per cent of equity of Indian Airlines out of which 26 per cent of the equity would be given to a strategic partner who whould be given a free hand in the management under the supervision of board of directors. Remaining 25% of the equity would be offered to employees, financial institutions and public.




records.name: ANANTRAY DEVSHANKER DAVE
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that Government have taken a decision to go ahead with disinvestment of some oil public sector units;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(a) whether it is also a fact that his Ministry has opposed the decision of Government in this regard; and

(b) if so, the details thereof and whether his Ministry was not consulted prior to this decision?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS ( SHRI E. PONNUSWAMY )


(a) to (d) : Government has decided to disinvest upto 10% of equity in Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) during the current financial year after the restructuring of stand-alone refining companies is completed. The decision has been taken in consultation with Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
